newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks to watch Wall Street next week.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks to watch Wall Street next week.

text.p: South African stocks, battered on Friday by a steep fall on Wall Street, will be watching New York shares closely next week for any signs the United State's market may be faltering, dealers and portfolio managers said on Friday.
A renewed bout of panic over interest rates sliced 160 points off the Dow Industrials index on Thursday -- the market's fifth largest points fall ever.

The delivery of Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget on Wednesday made South African shares particularly vulnerable to such fluctuations as investors, saturated with local facts and figures, looked abroad for future guidance.

"People will be looking very closely at what Wall Street will be doing. With the budget safely out of the way there are not many local factors for people to focus on," said one portfolio manager who declined to be named.
But most share watchers think that the Wall Street fall will be a temporary setback and shares will start to rise again, continuing an astonishing bull run on the U.S. market.
If that is the case, the South African market could offer some good selective buying opportunities next week as dealers will swoop to take advantage of the temporary dip.
"The market isn't cheap, but we are still selectively positive. There are buying opportunities in the market," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.
Economists see South Africa's fundamentals as strong and that view has been boosted by the positive reception given to Manuel's maiden budget.
An easing of foreign exchange controls and promises to reign in spending all impressed investors and have led to a firm currency and strong bond market.

But trade at the start of next week is likely to be cautious with the close-out of March futures contract on Monday. Derivatives traders will be rushing to close their positions, leaving the share market open to extreme volatility.
"People will be staying out of the market on Monday, apart from the futures traders," Scott said.
There are no major economic figures coming out next week, but several major companies are publishing financial results.
On Monday Anglo American Industrial Corp Ltd will reveal year results, followed on Wednesday by JCI Ltd's interim figures and Omnia Ltd's year numbers.
